design.description: Architecture and what shape a correct implementation should take

decision.description: Unresolved tradeoffs that would change persistence, deployment, integration, or an irreversible route

minimal-change.description: Whether the smallest correct change is enough, and whether extra complexity can be deleted

documents.description: Review of documentation, operator guidance, and other human-facing prose

ui.description: UI, accessibility, responsive layout, and design-system fit

adversarial.description: Work that is irreversible, internally conflicting, or likely to fail when executed, and needs a review that tries to break it

forager-smart.description: Use only for implementation involving state ownership or invariants spanning multiple subsystems, or an explicitly unresolved design choice. It implements the selected solution. Do not dispatch for review or research.

forager-capable.description: Use only when acceptance depends on generated artifacts, live probes, or a reproduce-diagnose-verify loop. Also use for standalone verification that requires live command execution. Do not dispatch for strategy, review, research, or ordinary implementation.

forager-documents.description: Use when the main deliverable is documentation, operator guidance, specs, reports, or other substantial human-facing text. forager-worker still owns code changes where documentation is incidental. Do not dispatch for code review.

forager-fast.description: Use only for mechanical, behavior-preserving edits such as formatting, renames, import cleanup, or generated snapshots. Do not dispatch for behavior changes, review, research, or UI-primary work.

forager-ui.description: Use when the main change is user-visible interface behavior, layout, styling, accessibility, React or component state, or UX polish. forager-worker still owns backend work and incidental UI text. Do not dispatch for review-only tasks.

plan-reviewer-xhigh-reasoning.description: Use when a plan has cross-system sequencing, irreversible migration risk, conflicting requirements, or a worker handoff that is likely to fail. It returns plan blockers; it does not give architecture advice or review code. plan-reviewer still owns routine completeness, missing detail, and general quality checks.

adversarial-plan-reviewer.description: Use when a Hive plan has irreversible steps, conflicting requirements, dependency races, or a worker is likely to execute the wrong thing. It reviews the plan as a worker handoff and looks for evidence that sequencing, references, assumptions, acceptance criteria, or verification cannot be executed as written. Return OKAY or REJECT; reject only for real worker blockers. plan-reviewer still owns ordinary completeness review.

ui-reviewer.description: Use when the primary review risk is user-visible behavior, accessibility, responsive layout, frontend state, visual regression, or design-system fit. code-reviewer still owns general correctness and backend review, including diffs where UI is incidental.

documentation-reviewer.description: Use when the diff is mostly prose: setup flow, operator guidance, terminology, or human-facing documentation. code-reviewer still owns diffs whose primary risk is code correctness, even if docs changed too.

adversarial-documentation-reviewer.description: Use when operators will treat the docs as the contract for install, deploy, or recovery. It checks guidance, terminology, and human-facing docs against evidence, looking for missing prerequisites, unrun commands, false claims, and misleading workflow. documentation-reviewer still owns ordinary prose and terminology review.

code-reviewer-xhigh-reasoning.description: Use when the diff has a concrete high-risk concern: security boundary, data loss, concurrency race, migration correctness, or public API breakage. It reviews the diff against the task and does not redesign the approach. code-reviewer still owns routine diffs, style, tests, docs, UI, and general correctness.

adversarial-code-reviewer.description: Use only when the diff can lose data, persist invalid state, or break a public contract. Probe adversarial cases within that concrete risk boundary.

adversarial-simplicity-reviewer.description: Use when a completed change added layers, flags, adapters, or defensive branches beyond the accepted task. It looks for YAGNI, dead code, duplicate logic, speculative abstractions, fallback branches, and unnecessary compatibility paths, and recommends deletions that preserve behavior. It does not redesign the approach or review correctness beyond unnecessary complexity. simplicity-reviewer still owns ordinary cleanup.

approach-advisor-xhigh-reasoning.description: Use when a concrete decision would change architecture, persistence, deployment, or integration boundaries. It advises; it does not approve plans, review diffs, or implement. approach-advisor still owns ordinary planning advice and local tradeoffs. If no concrete boundary-changing decision is on the table, stay with approach-advisor.

adversarial-approach-advisor.description: Use when the chosen route is costly to reverse, or competing routes remain plausible. It challenges an architecture route, migration, persistence boundary, deployment path, integration design, or hard tradeoff. It does not approve plans or review diffs. approach-advisor still owns ordinary advisory work.

ui-design-advisor.description: Use before planning when audience, information hierarchy, surface structure, interaction model, what the screen should emphasize, or design-system direction is still unresolved. It produces a design brief. It does not implement or review code. approach-advisor still owns questions that are not UI or UX direction.

scout-researcher-capable.description: Use when one research question needs multi-stage tracing, reconciling conflicting evidence, or correlating sources that do not fit one bounded lookup. scout-researcher still owns simple or well-bounded research. Independent questions should still be fanned out rather than folded into this agent.

scout-researcher-code.description: Use only for local codebase investigations that require multi-hop symbol or call tracing across multiple modules, or architecture mapping across component boundaries. Do not dispatch for bounded lookups, implementation, or review.

scout-researcher.description: Default for bounded routine research, local code lookup, codebase exploration, and external docs or data retrieval.

forager-worker.description: Default for ordinary implementation, bug fixes, and refactoring in an isolated worktree.

plan-reviewer.description: Default for ordinary plan review covering worker readiness, references, dependencies, and executable verification.

code-reviewer.description: Default for ordinary implementation review covering correctness, tests, risk, scope creep, YAGNI, and dead code.

simplicity-reviewer.description: Default for ordinary post-implementation simplicity review covering unnecessary abstractions, duplication, dead code, and safe deletion.

approach-advisor.description: Default for ordinary read-only approach advice on technical direction, architecture, debugging, and tradeoffs.

vulnerability-reviewer.description: Default for application-security review focused on evidenced attacker-to-impact paths and root-cause triage.
